# R2: Player-season profiles

*Generated by `python -m recruit.run_r2` from `results/r2_profiles_summary.json`. Do not edit the
numbers by hand.*

Data: StatsBomb Open Data (github.com/hudl/open-data), used under the StatsBomb Public Data User
Agreement. This page shows only summaries and the case player's own season profile, never event-level
data or other players' rows. The StatsBomb logo will be added before anything is published (NOTES.md).

## What this step does, in plain words

R2 turns 5,301,066 player events into one row per player for the 2015/16 season. For
each player it works out the minutes he played (from the lineup spells, added time included), counts
what he did (tackles won, pressures, progressive passes and so on, defined in `config/metrics.yaml`)
and expresses each count per 90 minutes. Defensive counts are also given **adjusted for possession**:
a player whose team rarely has the ball gets more chances to defend, so each match's defensive count
is scaled to what it would be with 50/50 possession (adjusted = raw * reference_opponent_share / opponent_share  (opponent_share = 1 - team share)), then summed over the
season. Raw per-90 values are kept alongside.

Each player gets a **role** (for example "Central midfielder") from the StatsBomb positions he played
most minutes in (`config/roles.yaml`). Players who changed club during the season keep one row with
their minutes for every club; there are 103 of them (38
moved between leagues in scope, 77 reach the minutes threshold).

These are descriptions of what players did in one season under stated assumptions, not predictions
of how they would do elsewhere.

Of the 7 possession-adjusted defensive metrics (fouls committed included, where
a low rank is not a weakness), 4 put him in the top quarter of his role pool.
In the matches he played, his team's possession share averaged 41.8% (weighted by his
minutes). Below 50% the adjustment scales his defensive counts down (more opponent possession meant more
chances to defend), above 50% it scales them up; both versions are shown.

## Possession: how it is measured and how well two methods agree

A team's possession share in a match is the share of in-play time inside its own possession sequences
(from each sequence's first event to its last event's end; stoppages and administrative events left
out). 252 events whose timestamp jumps back to about 0:00 although they come
at the end of the half in StatsBomb's event order are left out of the timing; without that rule one
such event stretches a sequence over the whole half (rule and reason in `config/profiles.yaml`). As a
check, the share of the match's passes made by the team was computed too. Over
3,034 team-matches:

| Agreement measure | Value |
|---|---:|
| Correlation between the two shares | 0.98 |
| Mean absolute difference | 1.7% |
| Median absolute difference | 1.4% |
| 95th percentile of the difference | 4.2% |
| Largest difference | 18.2% |
| Lowest / highest in-play share | 20.1% / 79.9% |
| Adjustment factor range (defensive counts multiplied by) | 0.63 to 2.49 |

Differences are in percentage points of possession share.

## Sanity checks (reported, nothing tuned to pass them)

- **Minutes add up.** The minutes of a team's players in a match should be close to 11 x match
  length. Of 3,034 team-matches, 3,008 are within
  2.0%. Below the band: 0 had a red
  card, 1 had a temporary "Player Off" spell (injury
  treatment) and no red card, 0 have neither. Above the band:
  25, with 1,226.90 minutes more than 11 players
  could play (0.0% of all 3,176,030.55 minutes). These come
  from the lineup data itself: in the largest case, checked by hand, a player recorded as coming back
  after a "Player Off" spell and his replacement both stay on to the final whistle, so twelve players
  are listed. Spells are kept as recorded (TO VERIFY in NOTES.md). Ratios run from 0.98 to 1.08
  (median 1.00). Match length (added time included) runs from
  89.99 to 105.55 minutes, median
  95.07.
- **Every position has a role:** lineup spells without a role: 0.
- **Every period has a "Half End" event:** periods measured from the last event instead:
  0.
- **Events belong to players on the pitch:** player events in a match where the player has no lineup
  spell: 10.

## Where the numbers live

- `results/r2_profiles_summary.json`: pool sizes, metric percentiles (10th, 25th, 50th, 75th, 90th)
  by role, the possession comparison, the checks above and the case player's profile.
- `data/processed/r2/` (not in git, StatsBomb terms): minutes per spell, possession per team-match,
  player-match and player-season tables.
- SQL: `sql/r2_*.sql`; definitions and reasons: `config/metrics.yaml`, `config/roles.yaml`,
  `config/profiles.yaml`.
